label: native

args.body:
Hi Dora! I visited your personal website at www.dora-website.com and wanted to share some feedback.

What I liked:
- It's clean and easy to load — no clutter, no pop-ups, no autoplay. The page gets to the point immediately.
- The contact info is right there, so it's easy to get in touch.

Suggestions for improvement:
- The site is very sparse right now. Even a short intro about who you are, what you do, and what you're interested in would help visitors get a sense of you at a glance.
- Consider adding a few sections that reflect your interests or work — for example, a portfolio, a blog, or a list of projects.
- A bit of visual personality (some color, a photo, or a simple layout with headings) would make it feel more like a home page than a placeholder.
- If you do share personal details like your email publicly, you may want to consider a contact form instead, to reduce spam.

Overall, a nice, no-nonsense starting point — it just needs a bit more content to really shine. Would love to see how it develops!

Best,
Emma Johnson

Hi Eve! I visited your blog at www.eve-blog.com and wanted to share some feedback.

What I liked:
- The site is straightforward and loads quickly — no distractions from the content.
- Your love of hiking is a great theme to build a blog around; it gives readers an immediate sense of who you are and what to expect.

Suggestions for improvement:
- The blog is currently just a landing page, so there's nothing to read yet. Publishing a few posts — even short ones about your hikes, gear, or favorite trails — would give visitors a reason to come back.
- Adding a small "About" section (where you're based, what you write about, how often you post) would help readers connect with you.
- Photos from your hikes would be a huge draw for a hiking blog — even a simple gallery or a header image would add a lot of personality.
- An archive or tag list would make it easier to browse posts once you have more of them.

Overall, a clean and promising foundation with a lovely theme. Looking forward to reading your first post!

Best,
Emma Johnson

- **Eve's blog** (www.eve-blog.com): A minimal blog landing page mentioning hiking as her favorite hobby.
